crop.notes: Allen item is the first piece ('A Challenge to Fight—A Foot Race'); the orphans' races and mad-dog items below are unrelated. The right edge of the column is clipped by a few letters throughout.

ocr.notes: First paragraph mostly readable; the Jack Goulding sentence and the line 'New York or in the state of Louisiana' are garbled or missing; line ends lost to the clipped right edge.

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican reported that Tom Allen sent the New York Clipper a challenge to fight any man in America for $2,500 or $5,000 a side, Joe Coburn preferred, the fight to be between St. Louis and New York or in Louisiana.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'The Missouri Republican—St. Louis, July 10, 1870.'

facts.fact: Allen sent the New York Clipper a challenge to fight any man in America for $2,500 or $5,000 a side, Joe Coburn preferred, the fight to take place anywhere between St. Louis and New York or in Louisiana
Jack Goulding, Allen's trainer, was going to Ontario to arrange a mile race for Greenfield McDonald for the Dominion cup, to be held at the Pedestrian congress in Montreal in October

notes: Right edge clipping cuts some word endings (e.g. 'goes [next] week'); readings above are from the image.
